title: Characterization, Conservation, and Genetic Breeding of Winter Squash (Cucurbita moschata D.): Case Study of the Collection Maintained at the Federal University of Viçosa Vegetable Germplasm Bank
content: Winter squash (Cucurbita moschata D.) is a vegetable of high socioeconomic importance owing to the nutritional quality of its fruits, seeds, and seed oil. This study reviews the main aspects related to the characterization, conservation, and genetic breeding of C. moschata accessions maintained by the Vegetable Germplasm Bank of the Federal University of Viçosa (BGH-UFV). Studies on C. moschata germplasm have reported high variability, particularly in Brazil. Currently, Brazil maintains six Ccucurbita germplasm collections, kept in research and teaching institutions. The BGH-UFV collection, one of the largest in the country, contains approximately 350 accessions of C. moschata, mostly landraces collected from all over Brazil. As part of a genetic breeding program to increase seed oil productivity and improve the oil profile, studies have identified accessions with seed oil productivity of up to 0.27 t ha-1 and accessions producing oil with high oleic acid content (21 to 28%). The program emphasizes the use of genotypes with high potential for oil production. The transfer of alleles related to compact plant size to genotypes with high production potential has also been successfully emphasized in the program. The works involving the collection of C. moschata maintained by the BGH-UFV corroborates the importance of this germplasm as a source of alleles for improving seed oil productivity and the oil profile. They contribute to the elucidation of the genetic mechanisms of important production parameters of C. moschata and, the promotion of healthy diets and food security for the populations that produce and consume this vegetable.
